documents.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
documents.content: Microsoft Defender for Cloud combines Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) with Cloud Workload Protection (CWP). CSPM provides visibility and hardening guidance, while CWP uses security alerts and workload-specific Defender plans to detect threats.

documents.title: Cloud Security Posture Management
documents.content: Cloud Security Posture Management continuously assesses resources, subscriptions, and organizations for security issues. Defender for Cloud summarizes findings with secure score and provides recommendations that help teams reduce configuration risk.

documents.title: Cloud Workload Protection
documents.content: Cloud Workload Protection detects active threats by analyzing workload signals with Microsoft threat intelligence. Workload-specific Defender plans protect services such as servers, containers, storage, databases, and AI resources.

documents.title: Layers of an Azure AI workload
documents.content: Azure AI workloads commonly include model endpoints, retrieval services, application logic, data stores, and orchestration or management services. Security teams should trace sensitive data across every layer and protect each service and connection.

documents.title: AI workload security responsibilities
documents.content: AI workloads need traditional controls for identity, secrets, networks, and posture, plus controls for model inputs and outputs. Prompts, responses, retrieval indexes, model endpoints, logs, and cached data all expand the security boundary.

documents.title: Prompt injection
documents.content: Prompt injection attempts to make a model ignore instructions, disclose information, or perform unintended actions. Direct attacks arrive through user input, while indirect attacks can be embedded in documents or other content retrieved by an AI application.

documents.title: AI data leakage and model misuse
documents.content: Sensitive data can leak through model outputs, prompts, logs, caches, evaluation datasets, or retrieval sources. Model abuse includes generating harmful content, automating fraud, or using an AI workload beyond its approved scope.

documents.title: Threat modeling AI workloads
documents.content: AI threat modeling should examine model behavior, prompt and response manipulation, data exposure points, and misuse scenarios. Map identified risks to controls such as identity protection, network isolation, Prompt Shields, and content filtering.

documents.title: Defense in depth for AI workloads
documents.content: A defense-in-depth AI strategy uses Defender for Cloud for posture and workload protection, Microsoft Purview for data governance, Microsoft Entra ID for identity and access, and Microsoft Foundry for model guardrails and observability.

documents.title: Enable the AI workloads plan
documents.content: Enable the AI workloads plan in Defender for Cloud for each subscription that contains AI resources. The plan discovers Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Azure Machine Learning, and connected assets to build an inventory for posture assessment and threat detection.

documents.title: AI workloads plan settings
documents.content: Optional AI workload settings can capture short, redacted suspicious prompt evidence for investigations and integrate with Microsoft Purview to classify prompt and response data. Related CSPM, storage, database, and sensitive-data capabilities improve coverage.

documents.title: Data and AI security dashboard
documents.content: The Data and AI security dashboard centralizes discovered resources, protection status, recommendations, alerts, attack paths, sensitive data findings, and internet exposure. Use its top issues and closer-look sections to prioritize investigation and remediation.

documents.title: AI Bill of Materials and Cloud Security Explorer
documents.content: Defender CSPM builds an AI Bill of Materials that maps models, datasets, services, and dependencies. Cloud Security Explorer queries help locate deployed AI workloads, exposed resources, and vulnerable code repositories that provision AI services.

documents.title: AI attack paths and recommendations
documents.content: Attack path analysis connects configuration weaknesses to show how an attacker could reach sensitive AI data or services. Prioritize recommendations for managed identities, private endpoints, encryption, and vulnerable dependencies to break those paths.

documents.title: Runtime threat protection for AI
documents.content: Cloud Workload Protection analyzes runtime signals from AI services, containers, compute, and data stores. It can detect suspicious prompts, data exfiltration, model abuse, anomalous API calls, privilege escalation, and unauthorized outbound connections.

documents.title: Respond to Defender for Cloud AI alerts
documents.content: An AI alert includes severity, impacted resources, evidence, related entities, MITRE ATT&CK tactics, and recommended actions. Respond by updating alert status, investigating supporting evidence, or using automation rules and Logic App playbooks for containment and notification.

documents.title: Investigate AI incidents in Defender XDR
documents.content: Microsoft Defender XDR correlates AI alerts with identity, endpoint, and data signals. Review incident timelines, affected assets, related alerts, and Prompt Suspicious Segment evidence, then assign, classify, and track the incident through resolution.

documents.title: Guardrails and Microsoft Content Safety
documents.content: Microsoft Foundry guardrails use Microsoft Content Safety to evaluate model inputs and outputs in real time. They can flag, annotate, block, and log interactions that are harmful, ungrounded, sensitive, or inconsistent with policy.

documents.title: Prompt Shields
documents.content: Prompt Shields detect jailbreaks and direct or indirect prompt-injection attempts. Configure them to annotate suspicious input for observation or to annotate and block it before it reaches the model.

documents.title: Content filters
documents.content: Content filters classify prompts and responses for violence, hate, sexual, and self-harm content. Configure input and output thresholds according to workload risk, then connect the filter to each model deployment where it must apply.

documents.title: Blocklists
documents.content: Foundry blocklists enforce organization-specific policies for restricted names, identifiers, URLs, and code terms. Entries can use exact matching or regular expressions, can be bulk imported, and should be applied to both input and output filters when appropriate.

documents.title: Protected material and groundedness detection
documents.content: Protected material detection identifies proprietary or non-Microsoft text and code in generated results. Groundedness detection evaluates whether a response is supported by its source data. Both controls help reduce disclosure and unreliable output.

documents.title: Test and validate guardrails
documents.content: Use the Guardrails and controls Try it out experience to test built-in and configured protections with representative text, code, image, and multimodal cases. Compare annotations and blocks, verify logging, and refine thresholds based on false positives and false negatives.

documents.title: Choose and refine guardrails
documents.content: Choose controls according to the workload's users, data, purpose, and risk. Start with moderate thresholds or annotations, review observability data, and regularly update filters, blocklists, and actions as usage, threats, and policy requirements evolve.

documents.title: Microsoft Entra ID and least privilege
documents.content: Use Microsoft Entra ID role-based access control at the smallest practical scope for Foundry resources and dependencies. Strengthen privileged access with managed identities, Conditional Access, Privileged Identity Management, and recurring access reviews.

documents.title: Foundry project access
documents.content: Foundry has resource-level Azure RBAC and project-level roles. Grant project access only to active contributors, inspect inherited access from broader scopes, separate administrative duties, and align permissions across Storage, Key Vault, networking, and Defender for Cloud.

documents.title: Secure secrets with Azure Key Vault
documents.content: Store Foundry keys, passwords, certificates, tokens, and connection strings in Azure Key Vault instead of code or configuration files. Let workloads retrieve secrets through managed identities with least-privilege roles, logging, rotation, soft delete, and purge protection.

documents.title: Network isolation and Private Link
documents.content: Use network rules and managed virtual networks to control access to Foundry, and use Private Link for private connections to Storage, Key Vault, model services, and APIs. Configure private DNS correctly and restrict outbound traffic to approved destinations.

documents.title: Foundry diagnostic logging
documents.content: Enable diagnostic settings on Foundry and each connected service, then route logs and metrics to Log Analytics, Storage, Event Hubs, or a SIEM. Protect log access, enforce collection with Azure Policy, and retain data according to compliance and investigation needs.
